title: Year 5 spelling and grammar check practice sheet (parenthesis)
subject: English
source: Written for english/y5 lesson 48 (Year 5 spelling and grammar check practice sheet (parenthesis))
intro: Lesson 48: Consolidation: parenthesis with brackets, dashes and commas. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Mark
Effect
Example
rows: Olympia (in southern Greece) hosted the Games.
Nikias - against all odds - crossed first.

panels.title: The test
points: Does the sentence still make sense?
If yes, the punctuation is in the right place

model.title: Add: the winners received only an olive wreath (to Olympic winners)

parts.text: Main sentence: Olympic winners received an olive wreath.
Extra detail: no gold, no money

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Olympic winners - no gold, no money - received only an olive wreath.

keywords.def: extra information added to a sentence that still makes sense without it
a mark that sets off extra information with a pause
a quiet comment to the reader

questions.q: Add brackets: The hippodrome was used for chariot races. (a long racecourse)
questions.a: The hippodrome (a long racecourse) was used for chariot races.

questions.q: Add dashes for drama: The bridge was gone. (swept away in the night)
questions.a: The bridge - swept away in the night - was gone.

questions.q: Add commas: Kostas her brother was a wrestler.
questions.a: Kostas, her brother, was a wrestler.

questions.q: Core: add parenthesis to eight sentences about the Games, using each mark at least twice (portal response box or exercise book)
Extend: rewrite one sentence with each mark and explain how the effect changes
questions.a: For example: dashes make the detail dramatic; brackets make it quiet

questions.q: Stretch: write a short paragraph using a relative clause and parenthesis

options: The race about (192 m) was quick.
questions.a: B) The race (about 192 m) was quick.. Brackets need to open and close around the whole extra detail.
